title.latin: Dominica XXIV et Ultima Post Pentecosten
title.local: Dominica XXIV et ultima Post Pentecosten

verses.text: Verbum Dómini, quod factum est ad Michǽam Morasthíten, in diébus Jóathan, Achaz, et Ezechíæ, regum Juda, quod vidit super Samaríam et Jerúsalem.
Audíte, pópuli omnes, et atténdat terra, et plenitúdo ejus, et sit Dóminus Deus vobis in testem, Dóminus de templo sancto suo.

responsory.text: Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra majestáte ejus:
responsory.repeat: Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

responsory.text: Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.
Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

parts.title: Lesson from the book of Micheas

verses.text: The word of the Lord that came to Micheas the Morasthite, in the days of Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda: which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, all ye people: and let the earth give ear, and all that is therein: and let the Lord God be a witness to you, the Lord from his holy temple.

responsory.text: I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory;
responsory.repeat: And His train filled the temple.

responsory.text: Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.
And His train filled the temple.

verses.text: Quia ecce Dóminus egrediétur de loco suo, et descéndet, et calcábit super excélsa terræ.
Et consuméntur montes subtus eum, et valles scindéntur, sicut cera a fácie ignis, et sicut aquæ, quæ decúrrunt in præceps.
In scélere Jacob omne istud et in peccátis domus Israël.

responsory.text: Aspice, Dómine, de sede sancta tua, et cógita de nobis: inclína, Deus meus, aurem tuam et audi:
responsory.repeat: Aperi óculos tuos et vide tribulatiónem nostram.

responsory.text: Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph.
Aperi óculos tuos et vide tribulatiónem nostram.

verses.text: For behold the Lord will come forth out of his place: and he will come down, and will tread upon the high places of the earth.
And the mountains shall be melted under him: and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as waters that run down a steep place.
For the wickedness of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel.

responsory.text: Look down, O Lord, from the dwelling-place of thine holiness, and take thought for us. O my God, incline thine ear, and hear.
responsory.repeat: Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

responsory.text: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock.
Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

verses.text: Quod scelus Jacob? nonne Samaría? Et quæ excélsa Judæ? nonne Jerúsalem?
Et ponam Samaríam quasi acérvum lápidum in agro, cum plantátur vínea, et détraham in vallem lápides ejus, et fundaménta ejus revelábo.

responsory.text: Aspice, Dómine, quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina géntium:
responsory.repeat: Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.

responsory.text: Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ ejus in maxíllis ejus.
Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.

verses.text: What is the wickedness of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Juda? are they not Jerusalem?
And I will make Samaria as a heap of stones in the field when a vineyard is planted: and I will bring down the stones thereof into the valley, and will lay her foundations bare.

responsory.text: Consider, O Lord, how that the city sitteth solitary that was full of riches; how is she become as a widow, she that was great among the nations;
responsory.repeat: She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

responsory.text: She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks.
She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

verses.text: Et ómnia sculptília ejus concidéntur, et omnes mercédes ejus comburéntur igne, et ómnia idóla ejus ponam in perditiónem, quia de mercédibus meretrícis congregáta sunt, et usque ad mercédem meretrícis reverténtur.
Super hoc plangam et ululábo, vadam spoliátus, et nudus; fáciam planctum velut dracónum, et luctum quasi struthiónum:
Quia desperáta est plaga ejus, quia venit usque ad Judam; tétigit portam pópuli mei usque ad Jerúsalem.

responsory.text: Redémit pópulum suum et liberávit eum, et vénient et exsultábunt in monte Sion et gaudébunt de bonis Dómini super fruménto, vino et óleo,
responsory.repeat: Et ultra non esúrient.

responsory.text: Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus.
Et ultra non esúrient.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Et ultra non esúrient.

verses.text: And all her graven things shall be cut in pieces, and all her wages shall be burnt with fire, and I will bring to destruction all her idols: for they were gathered together of the hire of a harlot, and unto the hire of a harlot they shall return.
Therefore will I lament and howl: I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like the dragons, and a mourning like the ostriches.
Because her wound is desperate, because it is come even to Juda, it hath touched the gate of my people even to Jerusalem.

responsory.text: He hath redeemed His people, and ransomed them therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall rejoice in the goodness of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil
responsory.repeat: And they shall hunger no more.

responsory.text: And their soul shall be as a watered garden.
And they shall hunger no more.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And they shall hunger no more.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Basilíi Magni in Psalmum trigésimum tértium
paragraphs: Cum te appetítus inváserit peccándi, velim cógites horríbile illud et intolerábile Christi tribúnal, in quo præsidébit judex in alto et excélso throno; astábit autem omnis creatúra, ad gloriósum illíus conspéctum contremíscens. Adducéndi étiam nos sumus sínguli, eórum quæ in vita gessérimus ratiónem redditúri.

responsory.text: Super muros tuos, Jerúsalem, constítui custódes;
responsory.repeat: Tota die et nocte non tacébunt laudáre nomen Dómini.

responsory.text: Prædicábunt pópulis fortitúdinem meam, et annuntiábunt géntibus glóriam meam.
Tota die et nocte non tacébunt laudáre nomen Dómini.

paragraphs: From the Sermon of St. Basil the Great, (Archbishop of Caesarea-in-Pontus,) upon the Thirty-third Psalm.

Whenever the desire to sin cometh over thee, I would that thou couldest think of the awful and overwhelming judgment-seat of Christ. There the Judge shall sit upon a throne high and lifted up. Every creature shall stand before Him, quaking because of the glory of His presence. There are we to be led up, one by one, to give account for those things which we have done in life.

responsory.text: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem;
responsory.repeat: Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

responsory.text: They shall proclaim My might unto the nations, and declare My glory unto the Gentiles.
Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

paragraphs: Mox illis qui multa mala in vita perpetrárint, terríbiles quidam et deformes assistent angeli, igneos vultus præ se feréntes atque ignem spirántes, ea re propositi et voluntátis acerbitátem ostendéntes, nocti vultu similes, propter mærórem et ódium in humánum genus.

responsory.text: Muro tuo inexpugnábili circumcínge nos, Dómine, et armis tuæ poténtiæ prótege nos semper:
responsory.repeat: Líbera, Dómine, Deus Israël, clamántes ad te.

responsory.text: Erue nos in mirabílibus tuis, et da glóriam nómini tuo.
Líbera, Dómine, Deus Israël, clamántes ad te.

paragraphs: Presently there will be found, by the sides of those who have in life wrought much evil, dreadful and hideous angels with faces of fire, and burning breath, appointed thereto, and showing their evil will, in appearance like the night, in their despair and hatred of mankind.

responsory.text: Hedge us about with thy wall that cannot be broken down, O Lord, and shield us continually with the arms of thy might.
responsory.repeat: O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

responsory.text: Deliver us also according to thy marvellous works, and give glory to thy Name.
O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

paragraphs: Ad hæc cógites profúndum bárathrum, inextricábiles ténebras, ignem caréntem splendore, uréndi quidem vim habéntem, sed privátum lúmine: deínde vermium genus venénum immittens, et carnem vorans, inexplebíliter edens neque umquam saturitátem sentiens, intolerábiles dolóres corrosióne ipsa infígens: postremo, quod suppliciórum ómnium gravíssimum est, oppróbrium illud et confusiónem sempiternam. Hæc time, et hoc timóre correptus ánimam a peccatórum concupiscéntia tamquam freno quodam réprime.

responsory.text: Sustinúimus pacem, et non venit: quæsívimus bona, et ecce turbátio: cognóvimus, Dómine, peccáta nostra;
responsory.repeat: Non in perpétuum obliviscáris nos.

responsory.text: Peccávimus, ímpie géssimus, iniquitátem fécimus, Dómine, in omnem justítiam tuam.
Non in perpétuum obliviscáris nos.

paragraphs: Think again of the bottomless pit, the impenetrable darkness, the lightless fire, burning, but not glowing the poisonous mass of worms, preying upon the flesh, ever feeding, and never filled, causing by their gnawing unbearable agony lastly, the greatest punishment of all, shame and confusion for ever. Have a dread of these things, and let that dread correct thee, and be as a curb to thy mind to hold it in from the hankering after sin.

responsory.text: We looked for peace, and it came not we asked for good, and behold trouble. We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness.
responsory.repeat: Forget us not for ever.

responsory.text: O Lord (our God) we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.
Forget us not for ever.

paragraphs: Hunc timórem Dómini se docturum prophéta promisit. Docére autem non simpliciter promisit, sed eos qui eum audíre volúerint: non eos qui longius prolapsi sunt, sed qui salútem appeténtes accurrunt: non alienos a promissiónibus, sed ex baptismate filiórum adoptiónis verbo ipsi consiliatos atque conjunctos. Proptérea, Veníte, inquit, hoc est, per bona ópera accédite ad me, fílii, quippe qui per regeneratiónem fílii lucis effici digni facti estis: audíte, qui aures cordis habetis apértas; timórem Dómini docébo vos: illum scilicet, quem paulo ante oratióne nostra descrípsimus.

responsory.text: Angústiæ mihi sunt úndique, et quid éligam ignóro;
responsory.repeat: Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.

responsory.text: Si enim hoc égero, mors mihi est; si autem non égero, non effúgiam manus vestras.
Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.

paragraphs: This fear of the Lord the Prophet hath promised to teach. But he hath not promised to teach it to all, but only to such as will hear him not to such as have fallen far away, but to such as run to him, hungry for salvation, not to such as have no part in the promises, but to such as by baptism are born children of adoption, set at peace and oneness with the Word. Come, ye children, saith he, that is to say, Draw nigh unto me by good works, all ye who by the new birth have become the worthy children of light, hearken unto me, all ye who have the ears of your heart opened, I will teach you the fear of the Lord, even the fear of that Being of Whom we have just been speaking.

responsory.text: I am straitened on every side, and know not what to choose.
responsory.repeat: It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

responsory.text: For if I do this thing, it is death unto me and if I do it not, I cannot escape your hands.
It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Cum vidéritis abominatiónem desolatiónis, quæ dicta est a Daniéle prophéta, stantem in loco sancto: qui legit, intéllegat. Et réliqua.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri
paragraphs: Quando ad intellegéntiam provocámur, mýsticum monstrátur esse quod dictum est. Légimus autem in Daniéle hoc modo: Et in dimídio hebdómadis auferétur sacrifícium et libámina; et in templo abominátio desolatiónum erit, usque ad consummatiónem témporis, et consummátio dábitur super solitúdinem.

responsory.text: Laudábilis pópulus,
responsory.repeat: Quem Dóminus exercítuum benedíxit dicens: Opus mánuum meárum tu es, heréditas mea Israël.

responsory.text: Beáta gens, cujus est Dóminus Deus, pópulus eléctus in hereditátem.
Quem Dóminus exercítuum benedíxit dicens: Opus mánuum meárum tu es, heréditas mea Israël.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: At that time, Jesus said unto his disciples: When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, stand in the Holy Place, (whoso readeth, let him understand.) And so on.

parts.title: Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)
parts.source: Bk. IV Comm. on Matth. XXIV
paragraphs: This injunction to whoso readeth, to understand, showeth that there is here something mysterious. In Daniel we read as followeth: “And in the midst of the week the sacrifice and the oblations shall be taken away and in the temple there shall be the abomination of desolation, even until the consummation of the time and a consummation shall be given to the desolation.” (ix. 27.)

responsory.text: Blessed is the people
responsory.repeat: Whom the Lord of hosts hath blessed, saying O Israel thou art the work of Mine own hands, thou art Mine own inheritance.

responsory.text: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, and the people whom He hath chosen for His own inheritance.
Whom the Lord of hosts hath blessed, saying O Israel thou art the work of Mine own hands, thou art Mine own inheritance.

paragraphs: De hoc et Apóstolus lóquitur, quod homo iniquitátis, et adversárius elevándus sit contra omne quod dícitur Deus et cólitur; ita ut áudeat stare in templo Dei, et osténdere quod ipse sit Deus: cujus advéntus secúndum operatiónem sátanæ déstruat eos, et ad Dei solitúdinem rédigat, qui se suscéperint.

responsory.text: Misit Dóminus Angelum suum et conclúsit ora leónum,
responsory.repeat: Et non contaminavérunt, quia coram eo injustítia invénta non est in me.

responsory.text: Misit Deus misericórdiam suam et veritátem suam: ánimam meam erípuit de médio catulórum leónum.
Et non contaminavérunt, quia coram eo injustítia invénta non est in me.

paragraphs: It is of this same thing that the Apostle speaketh, when he saith that a man of iniquity, even an adversary, shall be exalted against whatsoever is called God, or is worshipped so that he shall even dare to stand in the temple of God, and to show himself as God whose coming shall, according to the working of Satan, destroy and banish away from God all who shall receive him.

responsory.text: The Lord hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that
responsory.repeat: They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

responsory.text: God hath sent forth His mercy and His truth, (and delivered) my soul from among the lions' whelps.
They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

paragraphs: Potest autem simpliciter aut de Antichristo accipi, aut de imagine Cæsaris, quam Pilátus pósuit in templo, aut de Hadriáni equestri státua, quæ in ipso sancto sanctórum loco usque in præséntem diem stetit. Abominátio quoque secúndum veterem Scripturam idolum nuncupátur; et idcirco additur, desolatiónis, quod in desolato templo atque destructo idolum positum sit.

responsory.text: Indicábo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum aut quid Dóminus requírat a te:
responsory.repeat: Fácere judícium et justítiam et sollícitum ambuláre cum Deo tuo.

responsory.text: Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem, et inhábita terram.
Fácere judícium et justítiam et sollícitum ambuláre cum Deo tuo.

paragraphs: This prophecy may be understood either (first) simply of Antichrist, (secondly) of the statue of Caesar, which Pilate set up in the Temple, or (thirdly) of the statue of Hadrian on horse-back, which hath stood, even until our own day, upon the site of the Holy of Holies. In the Scriptures of the Old Testament “abomination” is a word very often used for an idol, and the farther title “of desolation” is added to identify an idol erected upon the site of the desolate and ruined temple.

responsory.text: I will show thee, O man, what is good, and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to
responsory.repeat: Do justice and judgment, and to walk humbly with thy God.

responsory.text: Trust in the Lord, and do good, and dwell in the land.
Do justice and judgment, and walk humbly with thy God.

paragraphs: Abominátio desolatiónis intelligi potest et omne dogma perversum: quod cum vidérimus stare in loco sancto, hoc est in Ecclésia, et se osténdere Deum, debémus fugere de Judæa ad montes, hoc est, dimissa occidénte littera, et Judáica pravitáte, appropinquare móntibus ætérnis, de quibus illúminat mirabíliter Deus; et esse in tecto et in dómate, quo non possint igníta diaboli jácula perveníre, nec descéndere et tóllere aliquid de domo conversatiónis prístinæ, nec quærere quæ retrórsum sunt, sed magis sérere in agro spiritualium Scripturárum, ut fructus capiámus ex eo; nec tóllere álteram túnicam, quam Apóstoli habére prohibentur.

responsory.text: Duo Séraphim clamábant alter ad álterum:
responsory.repeat: Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dóminus Deus Sábaoth: * Plena est omnis terra glória ejus.

responsory.text: Tres sunt qui testimónium dant in cælo: Pater, Verbum, et Spíritus Sanctus: et hi tres unum sunt.
Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Plena est omnis terra glória ejus.

paragraphs: But we may also understand by the abomination of desolation, any bad doctrine and when we see such a thing get a standing in the Holy Place, that is, in the Church, and showing itself that it is God, that is, pretending that it is His revealed truth, then will be the time when it will be our duty to flee from Judea into the mountains, that is to say, to leave the letter, which passeth away, and all guise of Jewish superstition, and to hie us unto the everlasting hills, from whence God doth right wondrously cause His light to shine forth. (Ps. lxxv. 5.) Then will it be our duty to find ourselves under a roof and in an house, wherethrough the fiery darts of the wicked one can never pierce to smite us, and not to come down to take anything out of the house of our old conversation, or to have regard unto those things which are behind but rather to sow in the field of the spiritual Scriptures, that we may reap thereof a bountiful harvest neither to have two coats, that thing forbidden to Apostles. (Matth. x. 10.)

responsory.text: One Seraph cried unto another:
responsory.repeat: Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.

responsory.text: There are Three That bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost, and these Three are One.
Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
The whole earth is full of His glory.

email.html:
The word of the Lord that came to Micheas the Morasthite, in the days of Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda: which he saw concernin…

Matins · Sunday, 22 November 2026

Dominica XXIV et ultima Post Pentecosten

Dominica XXIV et Ultima Post Pentecosten · Semiduplex

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

Lesson from the book of Micheas

Mic 1:1-2

The word of the Lord that came to Micheas the Morasthite, in the days of Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda: which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem. Hear, all ye people: and let the earth give ear, and all that is therein: and let the Lord God be a witness to you, the Lord from his holy temple.

℟. I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory; * And His train filled the temple.

℣. Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.

℟. And His train filled the temple.

Lesson II

Mic 1:3-5

For behold the Lord will come forth out of his place: and he will come down, and will tread upon the high places of the earth. And the mountains shall be melted under him: and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as waters that run down a steep place. For the wickedness of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel.

℟. Look down, O Lord, from the dwelling-place of thine holiness, and take thought for us. O my God, incline thine ear, and hear. * Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

℣. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock.

℟. Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

Lesson III

Mic 1:5-6

What is the wickedness of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Juda? are they not Jerusalem? And I will make Samaria as a heap of stones in the field when a vineyard is planted: and I will bring down the stones thereof into the valley, and will lay her foundations bare.

℟. Consider, O Lord, how that the city sitteth solitary that was full of riches; how is she become as a widow, she that was great among the nations; * She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

℣. She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks.

℟. She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

Lesson IV

Mic 1:7-9

And all her graven things shall be cut in pieces, and all her wages shall be burnt with fire, and I will bring to destruction all her idols: for they were gathered together of the hire of a harlot, and unto the hire of a harlot they shall return. Therefore will I lament and howl: I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like the dragons, and a mourning like the ostriches. Because her wound is desperate, because it is come even to Juda, it hath touched the gate of my people even to Jerusalem.

℟. He hath redeemed His people, and ransomed them therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall rejoice in the goodness of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil * And they shall hunger no more.

℣. And their soul shall be as a watered garden.

℟. And they shall hunger no more.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And they shall hunger no more.

Lesson V

From the Sermon of St. Basil the Great, (Archbishop of Caesarea-in-Pontus,) upon the Thirty-third Psalm.

Whenever the desire to sin cometh over thee, I would that thou couldest think of the awful and overwhelming judgment-seat of Christ. There the Judge shall sit upon a throne high and lifted up. Every creature shall stand before Him, quaking because of the glory of His presence. There are we to be led up, one by one, to give account for those things which we have done in life.

℟. I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem; * Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

℣. They shall proclaim My might unto the nations, and declare My glory unto the Gentiles.

℟. Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

Lesson VI

Presently there will be found, by the sides of those who have in life wrought much evil, dreadful and hideous angels with faces of fire, and burning breath, appointed thereto, and showing their evil will, in appearance like the night, in their despair and hatred of mankind.

℟. Hedge us about with thy wall that cannot be broken down, O Lord, and shield us continually with the arms of thy might. * O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

℣. Deliver us also according to thy marvellous works, and give glory to thy Name.

℟. O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

Lesson VII

Think again of the bottomless pit, the impenetrable darkness, the lightless fire, burning, but not glowing the poisonous mass of worms, preying upon the flesh, ever feeding, and never filled, causing by their gnawing unbearable agony lastly, the greatest punishment of all, shame and confusion for ever. Have a dread of these things, and let that dread correct thee, and be as a curb to thy mind to hold it in from the hankering after sin.

℟. We looked for peace, and it came not we asked for good, and behold trouble. We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness. * Forget us not for ever.

℣. O Lord (our God) we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.

℟. Forget us not for ever.

Lesson VIII

This fear of the Lord the Prophet hath promised to teach. But he hath not promised to teach it to all, but only to such as will hear him not to such as have fallen far away, but to such as run to him, hungry for salvation, not to such as have no part in the promises, but to such as by baptism are born children of adoption, set at peace and oneness with the Word. Come, ye children, saith he, that is to say, Draw nigh unto me by good works, all ye who by the new birth have become the worthy children of light, hearken unto me, all ye who have the ears of your heart opened, I will teach you the fear of the Lord, even the fear of that Being of Whom we have just been speaking.

℟. I am straitened on every side, and know not what to choose. * It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

℣. For if I do this thing, it is death unto me and if I do it not, I cannot escape your hands.

℟. It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

Lesson IX

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 24:15-35

At that time, Jesus said unto his disciples: When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, stand in the Holy Place, (whoso readeth, let him understand.) And so on.

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)

Bk. IV Comm. on Matth. XXIV

This injunction to whoso readeth, to understand, showeth that there is here something mysterious. In Daniel we read as followeth: “And in the midst of the week the sacrifice and the oblations shall be taken away and in the temple there shall be the abomination of desolation, even until the consummation of the time and a consummation shall be given to the desolation.” (ix. 27.)

℟. Blessed is the people * Whom the Lord of hosts hath blessed, saying O Israel thou art the work of Mine own hands, thou art Mine own inheritance.

℣. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, and the people whom He hath chosen for His own inheritance.

℟. Whom the Lord of hosts hath blessed, saying O Israel thou art the work of Mine own hands, thou art Mine own inheritance.

Lesson X

It is of this same thing that the Apostle speaketh, when he saith that a man of iniquity, even an adversary, shall be exalted against whatsoever is called God, or is worshipped so that he shall even dare to stand in the temple of God, and to show himself as God whose coming shall, according to the working of Satan, destroy and banish away from God all who shall receive him.

℟. The Lord hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that * They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

℣. God hath sent forth His mercy and His truth, (and delivered) my soul from among the lions' whelps.

℟. They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

Lesson XI

This prophecy may be understood either (first) simply of Antichrist, (secondly) of the statue of Caesar, which Pilate set up in the Temple, or (thirdly) of the statue of Hadrian on horse-back, which hath stood, even until our own day, upon the site of the Holy of Holies. In the Scriptures of the Old Testament “abomination” is a word very often used for an idol, and the farther title “of desolation” is added to identify an idol erected upon the site of the desolate and ruined temple.

℟. I will show thee, O man, what is good, and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to * Do justice and judgment, and to walk humbly with thy God.

℣. Trust in the Lord, and do good, and dwell in the land.

℟. Do justice and judgment, and walk humbly with thy God.

Lesson XII

But we may also understand by the abomination of desolation, any bad doctrine and when we see such a thing get a standing in the Holy Place, that is, in the Church, and showing itself that it is God, that is, pretending that it is His revealed truth, then will be the time when it will be our duty to flee from Judea into the mountains, that is to say, to leave the letter, which passeth away, and all guise of Jewish superstition, and to hie us unto the everlasting hills, from whence God doth right wondrously cause His light to shine forth. (Ps. lxxv. 5.) Then will it be our duty to find ourselves under a roof and in an house, wherethrough the fiery darts of the wicked one can never pierce to smite us, and not to come down to take anything out of the house of our old conversation, or to have regard unto those things which are behind but rather to sow in the field of the spiritual Scriptures, that we may reap thereof a bountiful harvest neither to have two coats, that thing forbidden to Apostles. (Matth. x. 10.)

℟. One Seraph cried unto another: * Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.

℣. There are Three That bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost, and these Three are One.

℟. Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. The whole earth is full of His glory.

Te Deum

Read in Latin and English

Sunday, 22 November 2026

Dominica XXIV et Ultima Post PentecostenDominica XXIV et ultima Post Pentecosten

Semiduplex

Lectio I

Lesson I

Incipit Michǽas Prophéta

Lesson from the book of Micheas

Mic 1:1-2

Mic 1:1-2

Verbum Dómini, quod factum est ad Michǽam Morasthíten, in diébus Jóathan, Achaz, et Ezechíæ, regum Juda, quod vidit super Samaríam et Jerúsalem. Audíte, pópuli omnes, et atténdat terra, et plenitúdo ejus, et sit Dóminus Deus vobis in testem, Dóminus de templo sancto suo.

The word of the Lord that came to Micheas the Morasthite, in the days of Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda: which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem. Hear, all ye people: and let the earth give ear, and all that is therein: and let the Lord God be a witness to you, the Lord from his holy temple.

℟. Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra majestáte ejus: * Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

℟. I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory; * And His train filled the temple.

℣. Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.

℣. Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.

℟. Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

℟. And His train filled the temple.

Lectio II

Lesson II

Mic 1:3-5

Mic 1:3-5

Quia ecce Dóminus egrediétur de loco suo, et descéndet, et calcábit super excélsa terræ. Et consuméntur montes subtus eum, et valles scindéntur, sicut cera a fácie ignis, et sicut aquæ, quæ decúrrunt in præceps. In scélere Jacob omne istud et in peccátis domus Israël.

For behold the Lord will come forth out of his place: and he will come down, and will tread upon the high places of the earth. And the mountains shall be melted under him: and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as waters that run down a steep place. For the wickedness of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel.

℟. Aspice, Dómine, de sede sancta tua, et cógita de nobis: inclína, Deus meus, aurem tuam et audi: * Aperi óculos tuos et vide tribulatiónem nostram.

℟. Look down, O Lord, from the dwelling-place of thine holiness, and take thought for us. O my God, incline thine ear, and hear. * Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

℣. Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph.

℣. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock.

℟. Aperi óculos tuos et vide tribulatiónem nostram.

℟. Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

Lectio III

Lesson III

Mic 1:5-6

Mic 1:5-6

Quod scelus Jacob? nonne Samaría? Et quæ excélsa Judæ? nonne Jerúsalem? Et ponam Samaríam quasi acérvum lápidum in agro, cum plantátur vínea, et détraham in vallem lápides ejus, et fundaménta ejus revelábo.

What is the wickedness of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Juda? are they not Jerusalem? And I will make Samaria as a heap of stones in the field when a vineyard is planted: and I will bring down the stones thereof into the valley, and will lay her foundations bare.

℟. Aspice, Dómine, quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina géntium: * Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.

℟. Consider, O Lord, how that the city sitteth solitary that was full of riches; how is she become as a widow, she that was great among the nations; * She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

℣. Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ ejus in maxíllis ejus.

℣. She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks.

℟. Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.

℟. She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

Lectio IV

Lesson IV

Mic 1:7-9

Mic 1:7-9

Et ómnia sculptília ejus concidéntur, et omnes mercédes ejus comburéntur igne, et ómnia idóla ejus ponam in perditiónem, quia de mercédibus meretrícis congregáta sunt, et usque ad mercédem meretrícis reverténtur. Super hoc plangam et ululábo, vadam spoliátus, et nudus; fáciam planctum velut dracónum, et luctum quasi struthiónum: Quia desperáta est plaga ejus, quia venit usque ad Judam; tétigit portam pópuli mei usque ad Jerúsalem.

And all her graven things shall be cut in pieces, and all her wages shall be burnt with fire, and I will bring to destruction all her idols: for they were gathered together of the hire of a harlot, and unto the hire of a harlot they shall return. Therefore will I lament and howl: I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like the dragons, and a mourning like the ostriches. Because her wound is desperate, because it is come even to Juda, it hath touched the gate of my people even to Jerusalem.

℟. Redémit pópulum suum et liberávit eum, et vénient et exsultábunt in monte Sion et gaudébunt de bonis Dómini super fruménto, vino et óleo, * Et ultra non esúrient.

℟. He hath redeemed His people, and ransomed them therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall rejoice in the goodness of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil * And they shall hunger no more.

℣. Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus.

℣. And their soul shall be as a watered garden.

℟. Et ultra non esúrient.

℟. And they shall hunger no more.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Et ultra non esúrient.

℟. And they shall hunger no more.

Lectio V

Lesson V

Cum te appetítus inváserit peccándi, velim cógites horríbile illud et intolerábile Christi tribúnal, in quo præsidébit judex in alto et excélso throno; astábit autem omnis creatúra, ad gloriósum illíus conspéctum contremíscens. Adducéndi étiam nos sumus sínguli, eórum quæ in vita gessérimus ratiónem redditúri.

From the Sermon of St. Basil the Great, (Archbishop of Caesarea-in-Pontus,) upon the Thirty-third Psalm.

Whenever the desire to sin cometh over thee, I would that thou couldest think of the awful and overwhelming judgment-seat of Christ. There the Judge shall sit upon a throne high and lifted up. Every creature shall stand before Him, quaking because of the glory of His presence. There are we to be led up, one by one, to give account for those things which we have done in life.

℟. Super muros tuos, Jerúsalem, constítui custódes; * Tota die et nocte non tacébunt laudáre nomen Dómini.

℟. I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem; * Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

℣. Prædicábunt pópulis fortitúdinem meam, et annuntiábunt géntibus glóriam meam.

℣. They shall proclaim My might unto the nations, and declare My glory unto the Gentiles.

℟. Tota die et nocte non tacébunt laudáre nomen Dómini.

℟. Which shall never hold their peace day nor night, to praise the name of the Lord.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

Mox illis qui multa mala in vita perpetrárint, terríbiles quidam et deformes assistent angeli, igneos vultus præ se feréntes atque ignem spirántes, ea re propositi et voluntátis acerbitátem ostendéntes, nocti vultu similes, propter mærórem et ódium in humánum genus.

Presently there will be found, by the sides of those who have in life wrought much evil, dreadful and hideous angels with faces of fire, and burning breath, appointed thereto, and showing their evil will, in appearance like the night, in their despair and hatred of mankind.

℟. Muro tuo inexpugnábili circumcínge nos, Dómine, et armis tuæ poténtiæ prótege nos semper: * Líbera, Dómine, Deus Israël, clamántes ad te.

℟. Hedge us about with thy wall that cannot be broken down, O Lord, and shield us continually with the arms of thy might. * O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

℣. Erue nos in mirabílibus tuis, et da glóriam nómini tuo.

℣. Deliver us also according to thy marvellous works, and give glory to thy Name.

℟. Líbera, Dómine, Deus Israël, clamántes ad te.

℟. O Lord God of Israel, deliver them that cry unto thee.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Ad hæc cógites profúndum bárathrum, inextricábiles ténebras, ignem caréntem splendore, uréndi quidem vim habéntem, sed privátum lúmine: deínde vermium genus venénum immittens, et carnem vorans, inexplebíliter edens neque umquam saturitátem sentiens, intolerábiles dolóres corrosióne ipsa infígens: postremo, quod suppliciórum ómnium gravíssimum est, oppróbrium illud et confusiónem sempiternam. Hæc time, et hoc timóre correptus ánimam a peccatórum concupiscéntia tamquam freno quodam réprime.

Think again of the bottomless pit, the impenetrable darkness, the lightless fire, burning, but not glowing the poisonous mass of worms, preying upon the flesh, ever feeding, and never filled, causing by their gnawing unbearable agony lastly, the greatest punishment of all, shame and confusion for ever. Have a dread of these things, and let that dread correct thee, and be as a curb to thy mind to hold it in from the hankering after sin.

℟. Sustinúimus pacem, et non venit: quæsívimus bona, et ecce turbátio: cognóvimus, Dómine, peccáta nostra; * Non in perpétuum obliviscáris nos.

℟. We looked for peace, and it came not we asked for good, and behold trouble. We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness. * Forget us not for ever.

℣. Peccávimus, ímpie géssimus, iniquitátem fécimus, Dómine, in omnem justítiam tuam.

℣. O Lord (our God) we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.

℟. Non in perpétuum obliviscáris nos.

℟. Forget us not for ever.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Hunc timórem Dómini se docturum prophéta promisit. Docére autem non simpliciter promisit, sed eos qui eum audíre volúerint: non eos qui longius prolapsi sunt, sed qui salútem appeténtes accurrunt: non alienos a promissiónibus, sed ex baptismate filiórum adoptiónis verbo ipsi consiliatos atque conjunctos. Proptérea, Veníte, inquit, hoc est, per bona ópera accédite ad me, fílii, quippe qui per regeneratiónem fílii lucis effici digni facti estis: audíte, qui aures cordis habetis apértas; timórem Dómini docébo vos: illum scilicet, quem paulo ante oratióne nostra descrípsimus.

This fear of the Lord the Prophet hath promised to teach. But he hath not promised to teach it to all, but only to such as will hear him not to such as have fallen far away, but to such as run to him, hungry for salvation, not to such as have no part in the promises, but to such as by baptism are born children of adoption, set at peace and oneness with the Word. Come, ye children, saith he, that is to say, Draw nigh unto me by good works, all ye who by the new birth have become the worthy children of light, hearken unto me, all ye who have the ears of your heart opened, I will teach you the fear of the Lord, even the fear of that Being of Whom we have just been speaking.

℟. Angústiæ mihi sunt úndique, et quid éligam ignóro; * Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.

℟. I am straitened on every side, and know not what to choose. * It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

℣. Si enim hoc égero, mors mihi est; si autem non égero, non effúgiam manus vestras.

℣. For if I do this thing, it is death unto me and if I do it not, I cannot escape your hands.

℟. Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.

℟. It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to sin against the law of my God.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)

Liber 4 Comment. in cap. 24 Matthæi

Bk. IV Comm. on Matth. XXIV

Quando ad intellegéntiam provocámur, mýsticum monstrátur esse quod dictum est. Légimus autem in Daniéle hoc modo: Et in dimídio hebdómadis auferétur sacrifícium et libámina; et in templo abominátio desolatiónum erit, usque ad consummatiónem témporis, et consummátio dábitur super solitúdinem.

This injunction to whoso readeth, to understand, showeth that there is here something mysterious. In Daniel we read as followeth: “And in the midst of the week the sacrifice and the oblations shall be taken away and in the temple there shall be the abomination of desolation, even until the consummation of the time and a consummation shall be given to the desolation.” (ix. 27.)

Lectio X

Lesson X

De hoc et Apóstolus lóquitur, quod homo iniquitátis, et adversárius elevándus sit contra omne quod dícitur Deus et cólitur; ita ut áudeat stare in templo Dei, et osténdere quod ipse sit Deus: cujus advéntus secúndum operatiónem sátanæ déstruat eos, et ad Dei solitúdinem rédigat, qui se suscéperint.

It is of this same thing that the Apostle speaketh, when he saith that a man of iniquity, even an adversary, shall be exalted against whatsoever is called God, or is worshipped so that he shall even dare to stand in the temple of God, and to show himself as God whose coming shall, according to the working of Satan, destroy and banish away from God all who shall receive him.

℟. Misit Dóminus Angelum suum et conclúsit ora leónum, * Et non contaminavérunt, quia coram eo injustítia invénta non est in me.

℟. The Lord hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that * They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

℣. Misit Deus misericórdiam suam et veritátem suam: ánimam meam erípuit de médio catulórum leónum.

℣. God hath sent forth His mercy and His truth, (and delivered) my soul from among the lions' whelps.

℟. Et non contaminavérunt, quia coram eo injustítia invénta non est in me.

℟. They have not hurt me forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me.

Lectio XI

Lesson XI

Potest autem simpliciter aut de Antichristo accipi, aut de imagine Cæsaris, quam Pilátus pósuit in templo, aut de Hadriáni equestri státua, quæ in ipso sancto sanctórum loco usque in præséntem diem stetit. Abominátio quoque secúndum veterem Scripturam idolum nuncupátur; et idcirco additur, desolatiónis, quod in desolato templo atque destructo idolum positum sit.

This prophecy may be understood either (first) simply of Antichrist, (secondly) of the statue of Caesar, which Pilate set up in the Temple, or (thirdly) of the statue of Hadrian on horse-back, which hath stood, even until our own day, upon the site of the Holy of Holies. In the Scriptures of the Old Testament “abomination” is a word very often used for an idol, and the farther title “of desolation” is added to identify an idol erected upon the site of the desolate and ruined temple.

℟. Indicábo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum aut quid Dóminus requírat a te: * Fácere judícium et justítiam et sollícitum ambuláre cum Deo tuo.

℟. I will show thee, O man, what is good, and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to * Do justice and judgment, and to walk humbly with thy God.

℣. Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem, et inhábita terram.

℣. Trust in the Lord, and do good, and dwell in the land.

℟. Fácere judícium et justítiam et sollícitum ambuláre cum Deo tuo.

℟. Do justice and judgment, and walk humbly with thy God.

Lectio XII

Lesson XII

Abominátio desolatiónis intelligi potest et omne dogma perversum: quod cum vidérimus stare in loco sancto, hoc est in Ecclésia, et se osténdere Deum, debémus fugere de Judæa ad montes, hoc est, dimissa occidénte littera, et Judáica pravitáte, appropinquare móntibus ætérnis, de quibus illúminat mirabíliter Deus; et esse in tecto et in dómate, quo non possint igníta diaboli jácula perveníre, nec descéndere et tóllere aliquid de domo conversatiónis prístinæ, nec quærere quæ retrórsum sunt, sed magis sérere in agro spiritualium Scripturárum, ut fructus capiámus ex eo; nec tóllere álteram túnicam, quam Apóstoli habére prohibentur.

But we may also understand by the abomination of desolation, any bad doctrine and when we see such a thing get a standing in the Holy Place, that is, in the Church, and showing itself that it is God, that is, pretending that it is His revealed truth, then will be the time when it will be our duty to flee from Judea into the mountains, that is to say, to leave the letter, which passeth away, and all guise of Jewish superstition, and to hie us unto the everlasting hills, from whence God doth right wondrously cause His light to shine forth. (Ps. lxxv. 5.) Then will it be our duty to find ourselves under a roof and in an house, wherethrough the fiery darts of the wicked one can never pierce to smite us, and not to come down to take anything out of the house of our old conversation, or to have regard unto those things which are behind but rather to sow in the field of the spiritual Scriptures, that we may reap thereof a bountiful harvest neither to have two coats, that thing forbidden to Apostles. (Matth. x. 10.)

℟. Duo Séraphim clamábant alter ad álterum: * Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dóminus Deus Sábaoth: * Plena est omnis terra glória ejus.

℟. One Seraph cried unto another: * Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.

℣. Tres sunt qui testimónium dant in cælo: Pater, Verbum, et Spíritus Sanctus: et hi tres unum sunt.

℣. There are Three That bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost, and these Three are One.

℟. Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.

℟. Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Plena est omnis terra glória ejus.

℟. The whole earth is full of His glory.
